note: f. la Tierra, the planet. Also soil and your home region: mi tierra.

sent.en: I fell to the ground.

note: f. luna de miel, honeymoon.

sent.en: There is a full moon tonight.

note: f.

sent.es: En el desierto se ven muchas {estrellas}.
sent.en: In the desert you can see lots of stars.

note: m. hace viento, it is windy.

sent.en: It is very windy today.

note: f.

sent.en: There is not a single cloud.
It is cloudy, it is going to rain.

note: f.

sent.en: Last night there was a very strong storm.

sent.en: It is thirty degrees.

sent.en: I brought you some flowers.

note: f. Also a factory or a power station: planta eléctrica.

sent.en: Water the plants, please.

note: m.

sent.en: What is your favourite animal?

note: m. Colombia has more bird species than any other country.

sent.en: There is a bird at the window.

note: m. Plural peces. A live fish. On a plate it is pescado.

sent.es: Vimos un {pez} enorme en el río.
sent.en: We saw an enormous fish in the river.

note: f. hacer una vaca, in Colombia, is to have a whip-round.

sent.en: There are cows on the road.

note: m.

sent.en: We walked through the woods.

note: f.

sent.en: The Amazon is an enormous rainforest.

note: m.

sent.en: There is a lake near the town.

note: f. Also, in Colombia, anger: me da piedra, it makes me cross.

sent.en: Guatapé has an enormous rock.

note: f.

sent.en: The sand is very hot.

note: m. Also a sports pitch.

sent.en: My grandparents live in the countryside.

note: f.

sent.en: I love being out in nature.

note: m. Colombians shorten it to el gym.

sent.en: I go to the gym in the morning.

note: m. Also a political party.

sent.en: Did you see the match last night?

note: m.

sent.en: What sport do you play?

note: f. Colombians also say balón for a football.

sent.en: Pass me the ball.

note: m.

sent.en: We went to a salsa concert.

note: m.

sent.en: Tonight we are going to the theatre.

note: m. The noun. To dance is bailar.

sent.es: El {baile} típico de la costa es la cumbia.
sent.en: The typical dance of the coast is cumbia.

note: m. in the singular, but las artes in the plural.

sent.en: I am very interested in art.

note: f. A television series.

sent.en: I am watching a Colombian series.

note: f. pl. Always plural for the news.

sent.en: Did you see the news?

note: m.

sent.es: Mi papá lee el {periódico} todos los días.
sent.en: My dad reads the newspaper every day.

note: f. The sport. To climb is escalar.

sent.en: Climbing is my favourite sport.

note: m. Colombians usually say it in the singular.

sent.en: These trousers are too big for me.

note: f. Also a football shirt.

sent.en: I am wearing a white T-shirt.

note: f.

sent.es: Lleva una {chaqueta}, en Bogotá hace frío.
sent.en: Bring a jacket, it is cold in Bogotá.

note: m. The Colombian word. In Spain a saco is a sack.

sent.es: Ponte un {saco}, que está haciendo frío.
sent.en: Put a jumper on, it is getting cold.

note: f.

sent.en: I like your skirt.

note: f. pl. In Colombia socks. Elsewhere it can mean tights.

sent.en: I need clean socks.

note: f. pl.

sent.en: On the beach I only wear flip-flops.

note: f.

sent.es: Ponte una {gorra}, el sol está muy fuerte.
sent.en: Put a cap on, the sun is very strong.

note: f. pl. gafas de sol, sunglasses. Colombians say gafas; some other countries say lentes.

sent.en: I cannot see a thing without glasses.

note: f. Also the woven Wayuu bag.

sent.en: I carry everything in my rucksack.

note: f. For clothes. Shoe size is número.

sent.en: Do you have a bigger size?

note: m. Same in the plural. Colombians also say sombrilla.

sent.en: Do not forget the umbrella.
